item.summary: This journal entry synthesizes progress in project proj-assumption-testing-epistemology by examining how neuro-symbolic rule-based frameworks provide error correction for models operating in novel environments.
item.title: Integrating Neuro-Symbolic Error Correction into Metareasoning Frameworks

inquiry_drive_shadow.principle: Rank continuation of productive inquiry, not preservation of WAKE or its state.

projects.title: Evaluation Frameworks for Autonomous Scientific Research

actions.assumptions_changed: Assumption that metareasoning operates solely via internal resource trade-offs without external rule-based error correction constraints.
actions.new_frame: Metareasoning and self-correction require integrating neuro-symbolic rule-based error detection to manage distribution shifts.
actions.old_frame: Metareasoning relies purely on static optimization of planning versus execution.
actions.reason: Integrate newly collected evidence regarding neuro-symbolic frameworks into the project's foundational assumptions.
actions.strategy: Extend assumption testing to include neuro-symbolic error correction mechanisms.
actions.trigger: Incorporation of new evidence on neuro-symbolic rule-based error correction in classification models.

review.alternative: Error correction might be achieved purely through end-to-end retraining rather than explicit rule-based systems.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing that pure end-to-end retraining outperforms neuro-symbolic rule systems across all distribution shifts.

claims.statement: Neuro-symbolic rule-based frameworks can be applied to conduct error correction and detection in models operating in unfamiliar environments.

support.explanation: The source demonstrates that neuro-symbolic methods provide explicit error correction mechanisms for models facing new environments.
support.passage: We provide a neuro-symbolic rule-based framework to conduct error correction and detection of these models to support eventual deployment in security applications.

actions.findings: Neuro-symbolic rule-based frameworks can be applied to conduct error correction and detection in models operating in unfamiliar environments. [source-f0124fd3eddc466d]
actions.limitations: The integration of physical error correction with cognitive epistemological models remains theoretical, and resource rationality accounts for biases are still under active investigation.
actions.next_questions: How can neuro-symbolic error correction rules be generalized to self-referential epistemological assumptions?
actions.reason: Revising the notebook to incorporate new evidence on neuro-symbolic rule-based error correction.
actions.summary: Neuro-symbolic frameworks offer rule-based error correction capabilities that complement resource rationality models by addressing environmental distribution shifts.
actions.title: Metareasoning and Robustness in Rational Agency
